questions.stem: Fill in the blank: She is ___ honest girl.
questions.explanation: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound (the 'h' is silent), so it takes 'an'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The sun ___ in the east.
questions.explanation: A universal truth takes the simple present; with the singular subject 'sun' the verb is 'rises'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: He is good ___ mathematics.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'good at' something.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: They have lived here ___ 2010.
questions.explanation: With a point in time (2010) in the present perfect, use 'since'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: I ___ my homework already.
questions.explanation: 'Already' signals the present perfect: 'have finished'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: There ___ many books on the table.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'books' takes 'are'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: She sings ___.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to describe how she sings: 'beautifully'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: He ran ___ than his brother.
questions.explanation: A comparison of two people uses the comparative 'faster'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: This is the ___ book I have ever read.
questions.explanation: With 'the ... ever' use the superlative 'best'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The children are afraid ___ the dark.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'afraid of'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: Please wait ___ me.
questions.explanation: One waits 'for' someone.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: Neither of the boys ___ present.
questions.explanation: 'Neither of' takes a singular verb: 'was'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: If it rains, we ___ stay home.
questions.explanation: A first conditional (real future) uses 'will' in the main clause.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: He has been working here ___ five years.
questions.explanation: With a duration (five years) use 'for'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: Each of the students ___ a book.
questions.explanation: 'Each of' takes a singular verb: 'has'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: I look forward ___ hearing from you.
questions.explanation: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition followed by a gerund.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: She insisted ___ paying the bill.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'insist on'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: Hardly had he arrived ___ it started to rain.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly ... when' is the correct correlative pair.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: He is one of the best players who ___ ever played.
questions.explanation: 'One of the ... who' takes a plural verb agreeing with 'players': 'have'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The news ___ true.
questions.explanation: 'News' is uncountable and takes a singular verb: 'is'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: I would rather ___ at home today.
questions.explanation: 'Would rather' is followed by the bare infinitive 'stay'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: He apologized ___ his mistake.
questions.explanation: One apologizes 'for' a mistake (and 'to' a person).

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: No sooner did he leave ___ the guests arrived.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner ... than' is the correct correlative pair.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The number of students ___ increasing.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' is singular and takes 'is'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: He was accused ___ theft.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'accused of'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: She is not capable ___ handling this.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'capable of'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The medicine had no ___ on the patient.
questions.explanation: The noun 'effect' (result) is needed, not the verb 'affect'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: He ___ his temper when provoked.
questions.explanation: The verb is 'loses' (to lose); 'loose' means not tight.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: They complied ___ the rules.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'comply with'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The teacher was annoyed ___ the noisy students.
questions.explanation: One is 'annoyed with' a person.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: Kindly ___ me of your decision by Friday.
questions.explanation: After 'Kindly' the base verb 'inform' is used.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: He is averse ___ taking risks.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'averse to'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: This behaviour is not consistent ___ his usual manner.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'consistent with'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: She has a flair ___ languages.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'a flair for'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: He was oblivious ___ the danger around him.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'oblivious to' (or 'of').

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: Success comes to those who ___ hard.
questions.explanation: In a general truth with the relative 'who' referring to plural 'those', the present-tense plural verb 'work' is used.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The scientist's findings were met ___ scepticism.
questions.explanation: The idiom is 'met with' (received a reaction of).

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: He is prone ___ making careless errors.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'prone to'.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The new rule is tantamount ___ a complete ban.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'tantamount to' (equivalent to).

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: Her account of the incident did not ___ with the evidence.
questions.explanation: 'Tally with' means to agree or correspond with.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The lawyer produced facts to ___ the false allegation.
questions.explanation: 'Refute' means to prove a statement wrong.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: He spoke with such ___ that everyone believed him.
questions.explanation: 'Conviction' means firmness of belief; the other words do not fit the sense.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The fresh testimony helped to ___ the accused of all blame.
questions.explanation: 'Exonerate' means to clear someone of blame.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: His arguments were both cogent and ___.
questions.explanation: 'Persuasive' pairs naturally with 'cogent' (convincing); the others have negative senses.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The manager was reluctant to ___ authority to his juniors.
questions.explanation: 'Delegate' means to entrust authority to others.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The reviewer's remarks were unnecessarily ___ and hurtful.
questions.explanation: 'Caustic' means bitingly sarcastic; the similar-looking words do not fit.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: She has an ___ for detail that impresses her editors.
questions.explanation: The idiom 'an eye for detail' means an ability to notice fine points.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: Had I known about the delay earlier, I ___ acted differently.
questions.explanation: This is a third conditional (past unreal): the main clause takes 'would have' + past participle.
